How to Measure – Step 1: Don and secure chest strap or smart shirt ensuring direct skin contact over sternum/ribcage.
How to Measure – Step 2: Power on sensor module and verify Bluetooth/telemetry sync with ISS biomedical laptop/tablet.
How to Measure – Step 3: Calibrate signal quality, confirm real-time waveform display, and wear continuously during duty/sleep.
What Does It Measure?: Autonomic nervous system activity, cardiac workload, and cardiovascular function.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Microgravity removes hydrostatic blood pressure gradients, causing fluid headward shift, stroke volume drop, and elevated resting/workload HR.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Transient resting bradycardia during first 24-48h, followed by compensatory upward shift (+5 to 10 bpm) and blunted peak exercise HR.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Persistent tachycardia signals dehydration, infection, hypercapnia, or deconditioning; bradycardia indicates excessive vagal tone or conduction defect.
Personal Baseline Definition: 30-day pre-flight seated resting morning average HR (± 5 bpm).
Watch Threshold: Resting HR < 50 bpm or > 90 bpm (or ±15 bpm baseline)
Watch Threshold Rationale: Indicates cardiovascular deconditioning, fluid shift, dehydration, or autonomic stress.
Act-Now Threshold: Resting HR < 40 bpm or > 120 bpm (or off-exercise > 160 bpm)
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Risk of acute circulatory failure, severe cardiac arrhythmia, or systemic decompensation.
Recommended Watch Action: Rest and repeat the pulse reading with good sensor contact. Check symptoms and record the trend.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Stop strenuous work, summon the crew medical officer, and assess symptoms immediately.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Motion artifact during physical activity; sensor displacement; dry skin poor PPG conductivity.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiovascular Health & Physiological Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Resting HR <50/>90 and <40/>120 are stated as validated astronaut limits; not substantiated by general NASA standard. | Recommended: Keep proposed baseline thresholds as DEMO ONLY; severe symptoms, consciousness and confirmed signal take priority over number.

On-Board Measurement Method: Resting 5-min ECG recording / optical wearable telemetry
How to Measure – Step 1: Assume quiet resting seated or supine position for 5 minutes in low-stimulation environment.
How to Measure – Step 2: Initiate 5-minute timed high-resolution resting ECG/PPG capture sequence via onboard app.
How to Measure – Step 3: Complete measurement without speaking or shifting position; verify R-R interval data integrity.
What Does It Measure?: Sympathetic vs parasympathetic autonomic cardiac modulation and baroreceptor responsiveness.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Serves as an objective, sensitive biomarker for accumulated operational stress, neuroendocrine exhaustion, and recovery quality in orbit.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Depressed rMSSD by 20% to 30% during spaceflight due to continuous sympathetic dominance, sleep fragmentation, and microgravity adaptation.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Pronounced rMSSD drop indicates acute autonomic strain, elevated allostatic load, fatigue, or operational stress; HRV alone cannot diagnose autonomic collapse.
Personal Baseline Definition: 14-day pre-flight standardized morning 5-minute seated resting rMSSD baseline.
Watch Threshold: Trend: RMSSD >20% below same-person baseline across repeated quality-checked readings (DEMO rule)
Watch Threshold Rationale: Marker of accumulated physiological strain, sympathetic dominance, or inadequate recovery.
Act-Now Threshold: NO STANDALONE HRV EMERGENCY RULE. Escalate based on serious symptoms or another independently verified risk.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Provisional trend threshold signaling marked autonomic strain; not an established medical emergency or definitive autonomic collapse alone.
Recommended Watch Action: Repeat HRV under standardized quiet conditions; review recent sleep, exertion and symptoms.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Do not activate an emergency solely from HRV. Escalate immediately if serious symptoms occur.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Highly sensitive to transient emotional state, recent caffeine, circadian timing, and respiration rate.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Autonomic Function & Cardiovascular Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 20% and 50% drops cannot establish severe autonomic collapse or be standalone emergency criteria. | Recommended: Use repeated baseline deviation as a nonurgent trend flag; no independent Act-now from HRV alone.

On-Board Measurement Method: Fingertip pulse oximeter / wearable optical sensor
How to Measure – Step 1: Clean and warm index or middle finger; inspect sensor emitter and detector windows.
How to Measure – Step 2: Apply oximeter probe firmly to fingertip; rest hand motionless on stable surface.
How to Measure – Step 3: Record continuous SpO2 and pulse reading after signal stabilizes for at least 30 seconds.
What Does It Measure?: Percentage of oxygen-saturated hemoglobin in arterial blood circulation.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Confirms systemic tissue oxygenation in sealed cabin environments vulnerable to ECLSS fluctuations, pocket hypercapnia, and hypobaric operations.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Mild transient reduction to 95–97% from cephalad fluid shifts, pulmonary capillary engorgement, and altered ventilation-perfusion matching.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Desaturation indicates arterial hypoxia, ECLSS scrub failure, toxic inhalation, atelectasis, or acute pulmonary impairment.
Personal Baseline Definition: Individual pre-flight resting room-air SpO₂ average (typically 97%–99%).
Watch Threshold Rationale: Early arterial desaturation; requires environmental verification and lung assessment.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Acute arterial hypoxia risk, life support failure, or severe pulmonary impairment.
Recommended Watch Action: Check sensor placement, repeat the reading and assess breathing and cabin oxygen conditions.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Call the crew medical officer immediately for persistent low oxygen readings or breathing difficulty; follow approved medical/atmosphere procedures.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Peripheral vasoconstriction, cold extremities, nail polish, or severe motion artifact distort pulse ox readings.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & Vol 2, Sec. 6.2 (Cardiopulmonary & Respiratory Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 90–94 and <90 are general clinical screening values, not verified ISS-specific safety limits; oximetry can misread. | Recommended: Confirm measurement quality; urgent symptoms or repeated low SpO2 warrant immediate onboard assessment; do not infer CO2 from SpO2.

How to Measure – Step 1: Rest seated/relaxed for 5 minutes; apply pneumatic cuff over bare upper arm aligned with brachial artery.
How to Measure – Step 2: Support arm at heart level without muscle tension; initiate automated inflation cycle on monitor.
How to Measure – Step 3: Remain still and silent during deflation; record systolic, diastolic, and MAP readings into health log.
What Does It Measure?: Dynamic systemic arterial pressure (systolic, diastolic, mean arterial pressure).
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Loss of gravity gradient alters central venous pressure and arterial baroreflex setpoint, precipitating post-landing and in-flight orthostatic instability.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Central blood volume increases acutely before plasma volume contracts 10–15%; resting blood pressure remains normal or slightly decreased with reduced diurnal dipping.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Hypotension poses syncope and cerebral hypoperfusion risks during G-transitions; hypertension exacerbates intracranial pressure and SANS progression.
Personal Baseline Definition: 30-day pre-flight resting seated brachial blood pressure average.
Watch Threshold: Repeated cuff SBP 130-139 or DBP 85-89 may prompt routine review; PPG BP class cannot be equated to mmHg
Watch Threshold Rationale: Early orthostatic instability or microgravity cephalad fluid shift; prompts hydration and garment check.
Act-Now Threshold: Extreme cuff BP >180/120 WITH serious symptoms, syncope or severe clinical concern -> immediate crew medical response; 160/100 without symptoms requires prompt review, not automatic hypertensive emergency.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Differentiates operational flight precaution (≥160/100 mmHg) from AHA-defined hypertensive emergency (>180/120 mmHg with acute target-organ symptoms).
Recommended Watch Action: Obtain a calibrated cuff reading if available; recheck and record symptoms.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Escalate immediately for serious symptoms with extreme BP or fainting. Do not diagnose an emergency from a PPG class.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Oscillometric cuffs sensitive to arm movement, improper cuff sizing, and microgravity arterial compliance shifts.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiovascular Standards & Hemodynamic Assessment)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 160/100 is not synonymous with hypertensive emergency; PPG category is not an oscillometric cuff measurement. | Recommended: Distinguish operations caution from emergency; >180/120 WITH concerning symptoms requires urgent assessment; verify with cuff.

How to Measure – Step 1: Cleanse electrode sites with alcohol prep pads; apply pre-gelled Ag/AgCl telemetry electrodes.
How to Measure – Step 2: Connect lead wires according to standard anatomical positions; power on ECG data acquisition unit.
How to Measure – Step 3: Verify 12-lead signal baseline stability, check for motion artifact, and transmit rhythm strip to MCC.
What Does It Measure?: Cardiac electrical conduction, sinus rhythm regularity, and cardiac ectopic activity.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Exposure to microgravity, electrolyte fluctuations (K+, Mg++), space radiation, and autonomic stress increases crew arrhythmogenic susceptibility.
Normal / Reference Range: Normal Sinus Rhythm (NSR), HR 60–100 bpm, < 1 PVC/hour
How Spaceflight Affects It: Increased incidence of benign supraventricular and ventricular ectopy (PVCs, PACs) triggered by fluid shifts and elevated circulating catecholamines.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Frequent or complex arrhythmias indicate myocardial irritability, electrolyte shifts, ischemia, or life-threatening conduction instability.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight 24-hour Holter ECG recording documenting normal sinus rhythm and absence of complex ectopy.
Watch Threshold: Isolated PVCs/PACs (> 5/min) or transient sinus pauses
Watch Threshold Rationale: Autonomic shifts and electrolyte imbalance can trigger subclinical ectopic activity.
Act-Now Threshold: Sustained VT, rapid AFib, or frequent polymorphic PVCs
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Critical arrhythmogenic risk and hemodynamic collapse requiring acute cardiac protocol.
Recommended Watch Action: Repeat the measurement; notify the crew medical officer about recurrent irregularity; obtain ECG if available.
Recommended Act-Now Action: For syncope, chest pain, severe breathlessness or sustained abnormal rhythm, activate the emergency response.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Microgravity motion artifacts, dry gel electrode degradation, single-lead limitations in detecting complex ischemia.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Cardiac Electrophysiology & Arrhythmia Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: PPG irregularity is screening, not ECG diagnosis; PVCs/min and VT labels require ECG. | Recommended: Use irregular-pulse flag prompting repeat and clinician review; serious symptoms trigger urgent protocol.

On-Board Measurement Method: LBNP orthostatic challenge (in microgravity) / Active stand test (1g/planetary surface)
How to Measure – Step 1: Pre-test rest: 5 min supine. Microgravity: secure in LBNP device; Planetary/1g: lie supine before standing.
How to Measure – Step 2: Microgravity: apply staged negative pressure (-10 to -40 mmHg LBNP); Planetary/1g: stand upright quietly with continuous HR/BP.
How to Measure – Step 3: Maintain protocol for 3–5 min with continuous telemetry; log heart rate, blood pressure, and any presyncopal symptoms.
What Does It Measure?: Baroreflex sensitivity, sympathetic vasoconstrictor reserve, and orthostatic tolerance.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Cardiovascular deconditioning and plasma volume loss in space impair cerebral perfusion upon re-exposure to gravity or during centrifuge operations.
Normal / Reference Range: LBNP/Stand: HR increase < 20 bpm; SBP change between -10 and +10 mmHg
How Spaceflight Affects It: Microgravity progressively degrades baroreflex sensitivity; astronauts exhibit excessive tachycardia and postural hypotension upon orthostatic stress.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Exaggerated tachycardia or precipitous SBP drop indicates orthostatic intolerance, severe hypovolemia, and high presyncope risk.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight standardized baseline LBNP response profile (-30 to -40 mmHg) and 10-minute active stand test.
Watch Threshold: HR increase > 25 bpm or SBP drop 15–20 mmHg during LBNP (orbit) or standing (1g)
Watch Threshold Rationale: Early orthostatic intolerance and diminished baroreflex response from microgravity adaptation.
Act-Now Threshold: SBP drop > 30 mmHg, HR > 130 bpm, or presyncope / syncope during LBNP or standing
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Severe orthostatic failure and cerebral hypoperfusion causing crew incapacitation.
Recommended Watch Action: Stop the test if dizzy, secure against falls and report symptoms; do not apply free-float standing thresholds.
Recommended Act-Now Action: If presyncope or syncope occurs, activate the collapse/urgent assessment protocol.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Conventional stand test is impossible in free-floating microgravity; LBNP is required on orbit, while stand tests are reserved for 1g/planetary gravity.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.1 (Orthostatic Intolerance & Neurovestibular Countermeasures)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Active standing is impossible in free-float microgravity; LBNP is not interchangeable with standing test. | Recommended: Specify condition: surface gravity/after landing vs LBNP in orbit; require adapted references and no automatic clearance.

On-Board Measurement Method: Infrared tympanic thermometer / ingestible core sensor pill
How to Measure – Step 1: Ensure sensor pill ingestion protocol or attach forehead double-sensor / inspect tympanic probe.
How to Measure – Step 2: For tympanic: align ear canal and depress trigger for 1-second infrared scan; for sensor pill: hold receiver.
How to Measure – Step 3: Confirm stable core temperature reading, log timestamp relative to circadian cycle and exercise.
What Does It Measure?: Core body thermal balance, metabolic heat storage, and circadian thermoregulation.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Impaired convective and evaporative heat transfer in microgravity leads to sustained elevated core temperature ("space fever") and heat strain.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Resting core body temperature resets approximately 1.0°C higher; thermoregulatory response during exercise is delayed with higher heat storage.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Pyrexia indicates systemic infection, sepsis, or heat illness; hypothermia signals environmental ECLSS failure or severe metabolic collapse.
Personal Baseline Definition: 14-day pre-flight circadian resting core temperature profile established across 24-hour cycles.
Watch Threshold Rationale: Spaceflight thermoregulatory shift ("space fever") or early systemic immune activation.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Severe systemic infection/sepsis, heat illness, or hypothermia emergency.
Recommended Watch Action: Repeat measurement with the same device and method; assess exertion, symptoms and habitat temperature.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Notify the medical officer for severe symptoms or confirmed dangerously abnormal temperature.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Tympanic readings operator-dependent; forehead heat-flux sensors impacted by local sweat layer; pill transit time variable.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & Vol 2, Sec. 6.2.4 [V2 6012] (Thermoregulation & Clinical Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 'Space fever' does not mean all high readings are infection; sensor types differ. | Recommended: Confirm method, site and exercise context; severe systemic symptoms trigger urgent assessment.

On-Board Measurement Method: Capillary fingerstick glucometer / minimally invasive CGM
How to Measure – Step 1: Cleanse finger puncture site with alcohol swab and allow skin to air dry completely.
How to Measure – Step 2: Perform lancet puncture on lateral finger pad; wipe away first blood droplet and apply second droplet to strip.
How to Measure – Step 3: Insert strip into calibrated POC glucometer; record fasting or 2-hour postprandial glucose value.
What Does It Measure?: Peripheral glucose regulation, circulating glycemic levels, and insulin sensitivity.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Physical inactivity, dietary changes, and chronic stress in space induce insulin resistance and altered carbohydrate metabolism.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Emergence of subclinical peripheral insulin resistance, elevated fasting insulin, and altered postprandial glycemic excursions.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Hypoglycemia (<60 mg/dL) causes neuroglycopenia, cognitive impairment, and syncope; hyperglycemia (>180 mg/dL) indicates metabolic deregulation.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight baseline fasting capillary glucose (average of 3 morning draws) and HbA1c.
Watch Threshold: Glucose <70 and >=54 mg/dL (ADA Level 1); repeated high values require contextual assessment
Watch Threshold Rationale: Emerging insulin resistance or Level 1 hypoglycemia (<70 mg/dL) requiring nutritional attention to prevent neuroglycopenia.
Act-Now Threshold: Glucose <54 mg/dL (ADA Level 2) or severe cognitive/physical impairment requiring assistance at ANY glucose level (Level 3); marked hyperglycemia plus serious symptoms needs immediate assessment.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Clinically significant hypoglycemia (<54 mg/dL) risking neuroglycopenic incapacitation or severe metabolic derangement (>250 mg/dL).
Recommended Watch Action: Confirm the glucose reading and contact the crew medical officer; follow the approved low-glucose care procedure.
Recommended Act-Now Action: If confused, unresponsive, seizure-like, or markedly low glucose, immediately summon help and use approved crew medical kit procedures.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Capillary fingerstick sampling sensitive to interstitial dilution and test strip moisture degradation in cabin air.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.6 (Metabolic Profiling & Endocrine Function Monitoring)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Updated <70 and <54 values align with ADA classes, but severity depends on symptoms and context; >250 alone does not prove DKA. | Recommended: Use ADA low-glucose categories with correct measurement and urgent assessment for altered mental status; no automatic drug/dose.

On-Board Measurement Method: Electronic food log (ISS FIT app) & barcode scanner
How to Measure – Step 1: Scan barcode of each food/beverage package using ISS FIT tablet scanner prior to consumption.
How to Measure – Step 2: Enter portion percentage consumed (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) and log additional water rehydration volume.
How to Measure – Step 3: Submit daily dietary log to synchronize macronutrient, sodium, and caloric totals with Mission Control.
What Does It Measure?: Daily caloric energy intake, fluid consumption, and macronutrient/micronutrient balance.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Anorexia of spaceflight and high operational tempo often result in chronic negative energy balance, accelerating muscle and bone degradation.
Normal / Reference Range: Caloric intake: 2,500 – 3,200 kcal/day (crew-specific); Fluid intake: ≥ 2.5 L/day
How Spaceflight Affects It: Voluntary caloric intake frequently drops to 70–80% of daily energy expenditure; fluid intake decreases due to blunted thirst reflex.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Prolonged deficits cause rapid lean muscle wasting, exacerbated bone demineralization, immune dysfunction, and impaired operational endurance.
Personal Baseline Definition: NASA nutritional prescription based on basal metabolic rate (BMR) and individual body mass.
Watch Threshold: Caloric intake < 80% target or fluid < 2.0 L/day for 2 days
Watch Threshold Rationale: Nutritional deficit accelerates muscle loss and hypovolemia impairs cardiovascular safety.
Act-Now Threshold: Caloric intake < 50% target for > 3 days or severe fluid deficit
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Severe catabolism, acute hypovolemia, and rapid neuromuscular deconditioning.
Recommended Watch Action: Review intake and hydration against individual plan; inform nutrition/medical crew if deficit persists.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Notify the medical officer if severe dehydration, inability to eat/drink, or concerning symptoms occur.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Subject to crew recall bias, barcode scanning omissions, and estimation error of shared or uneaten food rations.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.6 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.1 (Crew Nutrition & Food System Requirements)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Fixed 2,500–3,200 kcal and 2.5L are not universal prescriptions; low intake alone not emergency. | Recommended: Use astronaut-specific prescription; watch sustained deficits; urgent escalation depends on clinical dehydration/illness.

How to Measure – Step 1: Fasten Actiwatch device to non-dominant wrist and don dry-sensor sleep EEG headband before lights-out.
How to Measure – Step 2: Press event marker button when attempting sleep and upon final morning awakening.
How to Measure – Step 3: Dock devices into station laptop upon waking to offload sleep latency, duration, and architecture metrics.
What Does It Measure?: Total sleep time (TST), sleep architecture (SWS/REM), and sleep efficiency.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: 90-minute circadian orbital cycles, vehicle noise, and microgravity sleeping postures disrupt sleep architecture and induce cumulative sleep debt.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Sleep duration decreases to 5.8–6.2 hours on orbit; slow-wave sleep (SWS) and REM sleep are reduced and fragmented.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Chronic sleep restriction impairs cognitive function, psychomotor vigilance, decision-making, and emotional stability.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight 14-day actigraphy and subjective sleep diary establishing individual baseline sleep duration.
Watch Threshold: Sleep < 6.0 hrs/night for 2 nights or efficiency < 75%
Watch Threshold Rationale: Sleep debt induces neurobehavioral degradation, degraded vigilance, and crew fatigue.
Act-Now Threshold: Sleep < 4.0 hrs/night for ≥ 2 days or 24h acute sleep loss
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Critical psychomotor degradation, involuntary micro-sleeps, and high operational risk.
Recommended Watch Action: Review sleep conditions and schedule; avoid high-risk tasks while significantly fatigued.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Arrange immediate crew safety review if unable to remain alert for a critical activity; this is not itself a diagnosis.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Actigraphy overestimates sleep during quiet motionless wakefulness; EEG headbands prone to night displacement.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.3 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.3 [V2 7038] (Sleep & Circadian Entrainment)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Sleep <4h two nights is a task-safety escalation, not an emergency diagnosis. | Recommended: Use fatigue and task-safety restrictions pending crew evaluation; no automated prescription.

How to Measure – Step 1: Open computerized behavioral survey (B-CAT) on crew iPad during evening scheduled evaluation.
How to Measure – Step 2: Rate subjective mood, interpersonal cohesion, operational stress, and perceived workload on visual scales.
How to Measure – Step 3: Submit confidential response packet directly to Flight Surgeon / Behavioral Health Support link.
What Does It Measure?: Psychological well-being, emotional stability, operational stress, and crew cohesion.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Prolonged confinement, isolation, heavy workloads, and sensory deprivation heighten vulnerability to mood disorders and interpersonal friction.
How Spaceflight Affects It: Mood scores can fluctuate during mission mid-point ("third-quarter phenomenon") as psychological strain accumulates.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Marked mood decrements signal psychological distress, operational burnout, anxiety, or depressive reaction requiring clinical intervention.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight neurobehavioral evaluation baseline score across multiple standardized domains.
Watch Threshold: Score drop ≥ 2 points below baseline for 3 consecutive days
Watch Threshold Rationale: Early psychological strain, isolation stress, or crew interpersonal friction.
Act-Now Threshold: Survey score ≤ 3/10, acute panic crisis, or severe distress
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Mission-critical behavioral emergency, acute depressive reaction, or crew breakdown.
Recommended Watch Action: Offer confidential check-in, workload adjustment and optional support contact.
Recommended Act-Now Action: If immediate safety or severe psychological distress is reported, alert the crew medical officer under the privacy/safety protocol.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Self-report surveys subject to operational reporting bias, social desirability, and mission stigma concerns.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.4 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.4 (Behavioral Health & Psychological Support)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: One 1–10 survey is not a validated clinical screen; <=3 does not diagnose acute psychiatric crisis. | Recommended: Select validated brief instrument, include privacy and direct red-flag symptom checks; do not infer disease from a score.

How to Measure – Step 1: Launch standardized 3-minute PVT-B software protocol on crew tablet in a quiet environment.
How to Measure – Step 2: Respond as rapidly as possible to millisecond counter stimuli using dominant thumb press.
How to Measure – Step 3: Review mean response speed (1/RT), fastest 10% RT, and lapse frequency (RT ≥ 355 ms); log automated test report.
What Does It Measure?: Psychomotor speed, sustained attention, vigilance, and executive processing speed.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Cognitive slowing and lapse frequency directly threaten flight safety during complex maneuvers (docking, robotics, EVA).
Normal / Reference Range: Mean RT: 200 – 250 ms; 0 – 1 lapses (≥355 ms) per 3-minute PVT-B trial
How Spaceflight Affects It: Slower reaction times and increased attentional lapses occur primarily during high-workload phases, circadian desynchrony, and sleep deficit.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Increased response latencies and lapses (>2) indicate critical cognitive fatigue, hypercapnic impairment, or acute sleep loss.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight standardized 3-minute PVT-B baseline mean response speed (1/RT) and lapse frequency.
Watch Threshold: 3-minute PVT-B decline from individual baseline (15% or >2 lapses only DEMO threshold)
Watch Threshold Rationale: Psychomotor slowing indicating cumulative cognitive fatigue and circadian disturbance.
Act-Now Threshold: No validated medical emergency cutoff from PVT-B alone; stop critical tasks and assess when markedly impaired.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Profound neurocognitive impairment; immediate operational stand-down from critical tasks.
Recommended Watch Action: Repeat in standardized conditions; review fatigue and cabin environment.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Pause safety-critical tasks if performance is markedly impaired; request crew assessment.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Validated for 3-minute duration using ≥355 ms lapse threshold (vs 500 ms in 10-min PVT); sensitive to acute caffeine, fatigue, or display latency.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.4 & Vol 2, Sec. 10.1 (Cognitive Performance & Psychomotor Vigilance)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: PVT-B 3-minute cutoffs are not proven EVA safety limits; platform/device effects. | Recommended: Use PVT-B matched scoring and personalized trend; proposed 15%/35% thresholds only simulated.

On-Board Measurement Method: CEVIS cycle ergometer, T2 treadmill & ARED telemetry
How to Measure – Step 1: Connect heart rate chest strap and calibrate exercise hardware telemetry (CEVIS / T2 / ARED).
How to Measure – Step 2: Execute prescribed cardiovascular or resistive training protocol maintaining target heart rate/workload.
How to Measure – Step 3: Offload exercise performance telemetry file (power wattage, speed, total force, work volume) to ground.
What Does It Measure?: Cardiorespiratory work volume, aerobic power output, and resistive force generation.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Daily exercise countermeasures (CEVIS, T2, ARED) are essential to prevent severe musculoskeletal and cardiovascular deconditioning.
Normal / Reference Range: Aerobic: ≥ 30 min/day at 70–85% HRmax; Resistive: prescribed ARED load sets (100% compliance)
How Spaceflight Affects It: Exercise capacity (VO2peak) drops 15–20% without high-intensity training; mechanical loading must be artificially applied.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Low compliance or falling power output directly accelerates muscle atrophy, bone mineral loss, and post-landing disability.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight VO2max evaluation and 1-rep maximum (1RM) resistive loading profiles.
Watch Threshold Rationale: Under-dosing physical exercise risks rapid musculoskeletal and aerobic deconditioning.
Act-Now Threshold: Prescribed exercise missed for ≥ 3 consecutive days
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Acute acceleration of bone mineral demineralization and cardiovascular volume decline.
Recommended Watch Action: Review the planned exercise program and equipment access.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Notify medical/rehabilitation staff for inability to exercise due to injury or concerning symptoms.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: CEVIS and ARED telemetry measure mechanical load, not direct in-vivo muscle fiber tension or bone strain.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.2 & Vol 2, Sec. 7.2 (Aerobic & Resistive Countermeasure Systems)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: Missing 3 days of activity is not an acute medical emergency. | Recommended: Treat adherence as rehabilitation plan review, not urgent surgery/cardiac treatment.

How to Measure – Step 1: Collect fasting venous/capillary blood sample into specified EDTA/heparin collection tube.
How to Measure – Step 2: Centrifuge sample if required, load microfluidic analysis cartridge with plasma aliquot.
How to Measure – Step 3: Run automated cartridge in onboard POC bioanalyzer; record bone turnover markers (CTX, P1NP, Ca++).
What Does It Measure?: Systemic bone resorption (serum CTX) and formation (P1NP, osteocalcin) turnover rates.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Absence of weight-bearing loading induces severe uncoupling of bone remodeling, releasing skeletal calcium into circulation.
Normal / Reference Range: Serum CTX: 0.15 – 0.55 ng/mL; Total Calcium: 8.5 – 10.2 mg/dL
How Spaceflight Affects It: Bone resorption markers (CTX) increase by 50–100% within days, while bone formation markers remain flat or decrease.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Accelerated resorption indicates rapid cancellous bone decay, increased fracture vulnerability, and high risk of renal calculi.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight serum CTX and calcium panel drawn during baseline medical examination.
Watch Threshold: Bone resorption markers (serum CTX) > 25% above baseline
Watch Threshold Rationale: Accelerated osteoclast activity and uncoupled skeletal remodeling from unloading.
Act-Now Threshold: Serum CTX > 50% elevation or hypercalcemia (> 10.5 mg/dL)
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: High risk of renal calculus (kidney stone) formation and acute microarchitectural bone decay.
Recommended Watch Action: Repeat at the specified sample time and assay; arrange planned crew medical review.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Urgent response only for concerning clinical symptoms; isolated biomarker change is not an emergency.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Circadian rhythm in bone resorption; in-flight microfluidic cartridges sensitive to bubble formation in zero-g.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.2 (Musculoskeletal Health & Bone Density Loss Mitigation)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: CTX 25/50% changes do not alone indicate acute fracture or kidney stone; assay-specific ranges. | Recommended: Trend assay-specific CTX/P1NP with flight surgeon; acute concerns require symptoms/other tests.

How to Measure – Step 1: Collect morning unstimulated saliva using Salivette swab or obtain capillary fingerstick sample.
How to Measure – Step 2: Process sample in onboard centrifuge and insert test strip/cartridge into cytokine immunoassay reader.
How to Measure – Step 3: Measure concentrations of target cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha) and viral DNA copies; sync with ground.
What Does It Measure?: Pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-alpha, IL-1beta) and leukocyte distribution.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Spaceflight stressors (radiation, microgravity, sleep deprivation) suppress cell-mediated immunity and provoke latent virus reactivation.
Normal / Reference Range: IL-6: < 5.0 pg/mL; TNF-alpha: < 8.0 pg/mL; Normal leukocyte differentials
How Spaceflight Affects It: Persistent subclinical immune dysregulation with cytokine elevation, blunted T-cell function, and reactivation of EBV/VZV herpesviruses.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Cytokine changes are nonspecific; they must be interpreted alongside clinical symptoms, physical examination, and other laboratory findings.
Personal Baseline Definition: Pre-flight resting cytokine baseline and viral antibody titer panel.
Watch Threshold: Cytokine deviation vs own baseline (30% is DEMO ONLY); symptoms and assay consistency required
Watch Threshold Rationale: Nonspecific physiological stress or immune modulation; requires correlation with clinical presentation.
Act-Now Threshold: NO STANDALONE CYTOKINE EMERGENCY RULE. Escalate for severe symptoms or other verified medical red flags.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Possible active infection or systemic inflammatory process; not diagnostic of immune collapse alone without clinical signs.
Recommended Watch Action: Interpret with symptoms and validated lab-specific reference ranges; monitor per medical plan.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Activate immediate assessment for serious infection symptoms; avoid diagnosing infection from cytokines alone.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Cytokine changes are nonspecific; affected by circadian rhythm, exercise, and minor stress; requires clinical and laboratory correlation.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 3.1 & 4.7 (Immunological Dysregulation & Host Defense)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: IL-6/TNF changes are nonspecific; doubling cytokines cannot diagnose infection or 'immune collapse'. | Recommended: Do not use isolated cytokine elevations as emergency trigger; incorporate symptoms and other tests.

On-Board Measurement Method: Crew Passive Dosimeter (CPD) & Active Personal Dosimeter (APD)
How to Measure – Step 1: Wear active personal dosimeter (APD) on operational flight suit continuously during duty hours.
How to Measure – Step 2: Perform weekly optical/digital readout and dock APD with station radiation console.
How to Measure – Step 3: Inspect passive dosimeter badge (CPD) position and verify real-time dose rate alarms (<1.0 mSv/day).
What Does It Measure?: Ambient ionizing radiation exposure and absorbed equivalent dose from GCR and SPE.
Why Does It Matter in Space?: Space radiation outside Earth's magnetosphere produces cumulative DNA double-strand breaks, cancer risks, and acute radiation sickness risk.
Normal / Reference Range: Background in LEO: 0.3 – 0.8 mSv/day (< 1.0 mSv/day nominal); Career limit based on NASA Permissible Exposure Limits
How Spaceflight Affects It: Continuous exposure to galactic cosmic rays (GCR) and episodic solar particle events (SPE), yielding daily doses 100x higher than Earth surface.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Dose rates > 10 mSv/hr trigger operational storm shelter protocols; clinical ARS requires high total absorbed dose (>0.7 Gy), dose rate, and whole-body exposure.
Personal Baseline Definition: Cumulative lifetime radiation exposure record maintained by NASA Radiation Health Officer.
Watch Threshold: Mission radiation warning / rising dose relative to mission-specific limits; 1mSv/day DEMO ONLY
Watch Threshold Rationale: Elevated space radiation flux approaching operational exposure management thresholds.
Act-Now Threshold: Active spacecraft solar-particle-event or radiation shelter alarm (mission-defined); 10mSv/h is NOT an acute radiation syndrome diagnostic cutoff.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Operational radiation protection trigger during SPEs to limit cumulative exposure; distinct from clinical ARS which requires high absorbed doses (>0.7 Gy).
Recommended Watch Action: Verify the environmental alert and mission-set radiation constraints; review shielding/EVA status.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Follow the spacecraft's authorized solar-particle-event shelter warning and suspend EVA as directed.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Dosimeters measure physical dose/rate; clinical ARS depends on total absorbed dose, exposure duration, radiation characteristics, and body volume exposed.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1, Sec. 4.8 [V1 4029] & Vol 2, Sec. 6.8 (Space Permissible Exposure Limits & ALARA)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: 10 mSv/h should not be labelled ARS cutoff; mission limits depend on organ, duration, mission. | Recommended: Use spacecraft radiation-alert and storm-shelter signals with mission-set limits, not a universal 10 mSv/h ARS rule.

On-Board Measurement Method: ECLSS Major Constituent Analyzer (MCA) & portable sensor
How to Measure – Step 1: Power on handheld/portable optical CO2 sensor or query station ECLSS MCA telemetry channel.
How to Measure – Step 2: Take ambient ppCO2 readings at crew breathing height across multiple station modules/sleep cabins.
How to Measure – Step 3: Verify local ppCO2 is below 2.0 mmHg; verify adequate ventilation flow and cabin fan operation.
What Does It Measure?: Ambient spacecraft cabin partial pressure of carbon dioxide (ppCO2).
Why Does It Matter in Space?: In microgravity, absence of natural thermal convection causes CO2 accumulation around crew heads, triggering headaches and visual impairment.
Normal / Reference Range: Cabin ppCO2 < 2.0 mmHg (approx. < 2,600 ppm); nominal target < 1.5 mmHg
How Spaceflight Affects It: CO2 levels in closed spacecraft cabins run significantly higher than terrestrial atmospheric levels (0.3 mmHg), fluctuating with crew activity and ECLSS cycling.
Meaning of Abnormal Results: Elevated ppCO2 (>2.0 mmHg) is associated with astronaut headaches and SANS symptoms; clinical toxicity and narcosis occur at much higher terrestrial levels.
Personal Baseline Definition: Vehicle ECLSS baseline environmental limit specification (NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2).
Watch Threshold: Operational early warning at ppCO2 >=2 mmHg (DEMO CONSERVATIVE) or rising trend
Watch Threshold Rationale: Conservative operational watch threshold associated with increased risk of astronaut headaches and SANS exacerbation.
Act-Now Threshold: One-hour average cabin ppCO2 >3 mmHg violates NASA-STD-3001 Rev F nominal requirement [V2 6004]; environmental response per mission-specific procedures. Do not label 4 mmHg as CO2 narcosis.
Act-Now Threshold Rationale: Operational environmental limit requiring active scrubbing intervention; conservative flight rule well below clinical CO₂ narcosis.
Recommended Watch Action: Verify CO2 sensor, duration and local ventilation; notify life-support operators.
Recommended Act-Now Action: Activate authorized environmental response for mission CO2 alarm or symptomatic crew; do not equate 4 mmHg with CO2 narcosis.
Escalation Level: Conditional: watch = crew/next window; true emergency = now
Measurement Limitations: Localized air stagnation pockets in station modules may differ substantially from central ECLSS MCA sensor readings.
Scientific Source / Citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2, Sec. 6.2.3 [V2 6027] (Environmental Health - Cabin CO2 Limits)
Notes: QA 2026-11-14: NASA 2026 Vol2 Rev F specifies 1-hour habitat average <=3 mmHg; 2/4 are not validated medical severity categories. | Recommended: Label 2 mmHg as conservative engineering warning only; 3 mmHg 1-hour requirement, off-nominal response mission-specific.
